plan.notes: Source: Nassau Community College College Catalog 2020-2021 (official NCC catalog PDF, https://collegecatalog.ncc.edu/current -> http://collegecatalog.ncc.edu/_resources/pdfs/ncc_college_catalog_2020_2021.pdf), COMPUTER SCIENCE (A.S.) section, Hegis Code 5101, pp. 164-166. Catalog-year truth: NCC's true degree name is 'Computer Science (A.S.)' - AS verified, no substitution. Transcription method: manual transcription of the catalog's published four-semester sequence by reading the live catalog PDF in the browser and copying course codes, titles, and credits verbatim. Sequence totals are the catalog's own published totals (Sem1 17 + Sem2 17 + Sem3 16 + Sem4 14 = 64) which equal the catalog's stated Total Credits: 64 - no discrepancy. Caveats carried from the catalog: (a) Students who do not qualify for MAT 122 Calculus I and CSC 120 Computer Science I must seek advisement for MAT and CSC placement; more than four semesters may be required to complete the degree. (b) ENG 100 vs 101 vs 108 depends on placement (footnote 1). (c) HED Health Elective must be a 3-credit HED course, not a 2-credit course (footnote 2). (d) The two science courses must form a single two-semester sequence: PHY 151+152, BIO 109+110, or CHE 151+152 (footnote 6) - transcribe as two coordinated choice slots. (e) CSC/MAT Elective options per catalog footnote 5: CSC 240 Mobile Application Development; MAT 131 Probability with Statistical Inference; MAT 200 Foundations of Advanced Mathematics; MAT 225 Multivariable Calculus; MAT 226 Elementary Linear Algebra (requires MAT 123 prerequisite); MAT 234 Elementary Differential Equations (requires MAT 123 prerequisite); MAT 235 Algebraic Structures (requires MAT 225 prerequisite). (f) Social Science Elective (Sem1, footnote 3) must fulfill a SUNY GER (American History / Other World Civilizations / Social Sciences / Western Civilization); Sem3 Social Science Elective (footnote 7) must fulfill a different one of those than Sem1. (g) Humanities Elective (Sem2, footnote 4) must fulfill a SUNY GER (Foreign Languages / Humanities / The Arts / Other World Civilizations); Sem4 Humanities Elective (footnote 8) must fulfill a different one of those than Sem2. Per-course prerequisites are not published in the catalog's sequence section, so all prereq lists are empty rather than invented; stated option prerequisites are documented in the choice notes.
